(1) Some say one must, etc.; they used the language "some say" because Rambam disagrees on this as is explained in Beis Yosef; and see in Biur HaGra who rules like Rambam [and it requires further study in his words that he wrote that the conclusion of Tosafos is also like Rambam and it is not so clear in Rosh Hashanah there, and in Moed Katan daf 4a in Tosafos s.v. mah l'halan it is proven explicitly that they hold that tosefet Shabbos is d'oraisa; and perhaps he had a different text in Tosafos Rosh Hashanah; and also his seeing that he brought from what they said on Shabbos daf 18 that we permit with the sun is not the only [proof] according to his view who rules like the view of the Geonim that immediately when the sun sets from our eyes it is included in bein hashemashot, which is not so according to Shulchan Aruch; it is not proof at all]; and in Acharonim he wrote that for practical law we follow this "some say" because all the Rishonim hold thus [from the sugya in Rosh Hashanah 9 and Yoma chapter 1]; and likewise in Shulchan Aruch below in siman 393 seif 2 he rules anonymously like this "some say." And know that regarding the time of erev Shabbos there is not so much difference, for for both of them the prohibition of melacha begins after sunset and not before; and on the contrary, for the Gra according to his view it is more stringent, for according to him who rules like the view of the Geonim, immediately when the sun sets (namely from the hour when the sun is hidden from our eyes) it is included in bein hashemashot, and in this there is safek issur skilah, whereas tosefet Shabbos contains nothing except a mere positive commandment, and also it depends on his will during the time of 3 milin after sunset as is explained in Shulchan Aruch. And know further that d'rabbanan even for Rambam it is a mitzvah to add a little from the weekday onto the holy [day], as the plain meaning of the wording of Rabbeinu HaMagid which is brought in Beis Yosef implies. And what Bach challenged; if so Rambam should not have omitted this law of addition, for in truth he already included it in what he brought the law of the tekios which they would blow on erev Shabbos in chapter 5 [Keneset HaGedolah in the name of Ra'anach]; and likewise in Biur HaGra that even for Rambam it is a mitzvah to add from the weekday onto the holy from this that the aforesaid tekios [and ostensibly it appears that also on Motzei Shabbos it is a mitzvah for all to add from the weekday onto the holy a little, for departing Shabbos is not inferior to entering; except that for Rambam this would be d'rabbanan and according to Shulchan Aruch d'oraisa]. And accordingly for the Gra it is more stringent also in this matter, for according to him it is a mitzvah to add at least d'rabbanan a little before sunset; whereas according to Shulchan Aruch we do not obligate at all before sunset. And in truth per the view of the Geonim who stand in the view of the Gra regarding bein hashemashot, and as we will write below if they hold like the view of the Rif and the other Rishonim that tosefet is required (that which we learned "we permit with the sun") therefore it is not specifically with the sun literally but a little before because of tosefet, and per them there would be a concern of d'oraisa:
(2) From the beginning of sunset; the reason for all this is that in Pesachim 94 it states that from sunset until the emergence of the stars is the measure of 4 milin; and in Shabbos [34-35] it states that from sunset bein hashemashot begins [for Rabba according to R. Yehudah whom we rule like]; and it says there that bein hashemashot lasts three-quarters of a mil and afterward it becomes night; and we say there that three medium-sized stars constitute night. If so, there is a contradiction, and perforce Rabbeinu Tam and his camp answer to divide between sunset in Pesachim and sunset in Shabbos there, that the one in Pesachim is the beginning of sunset (from when the body of the sun is hidden when it sets from our eyes) and from then until the emergence of the stars is 4 milin; and when the sun sets in Shabbos there it is the end of sunset, which is when the light of the sun also sets from most of the sky toward the west alone; and from then bein hashemashot begins, which is three-quarters of a mil before the emergence of the stars. And from the beginning of sunset, which is the sunset of the body of the sun, until the end of the aforesaid sunset is day, and its duration is 3 milin and a quarter; and then is the time of tosefet Shabbos, as is written here in Shulchan Aruch; and among all of them they are 4 milin, and until 4 milin from the beginning of sunset it is not certainly night; this is the view of Rabbeinu Tam and his camp; and see below in siman 331 seif 5 in Magen Avraham, it appears there that his view for halachah is like this view; but the Gra z"l disagrees on this view and extended with several proofs that sunset in Shabbos regarding bein hashemashot is also the beginning of sunset like sunset in Pesachim there, and immediately after sunset of the body of the sun bein hashemashot begins according to R. Yehudah whom R. Yochanan ruled like stringently on Shabbos there; and the duration of bein hashemashot is three-quarters of a mil; and the aforesaid difficulty he answers to divide between the emergence of the stars of Shabbos and the emergence of the stars of Pesachim, that the emergence of the stars of Shabbos is the time of night which is three medium-sized stars, and the emergence of the stars of Pesachim is the emergence of all the stars visible at night, which is a much later time, and is 4 milin after the beginning of sunset. And even though it appears to the eyes that the duration of bein hashemashot until the emergence of the stars is much more than three-quarters of a mil, it is as the Gra wrote in his Biur that the measure of the Gemara is stated only regarding the horizon of Babylonia or Eretz Yisrael; and in our countries which are more inclined toward the north it lengthens more; and therefore regarding the end of bein hashemashot we do not have a fixed duration from the Gemara on our horizon, and it depends only according to sight when it is three medium-sized stars, but not large ones; and because we are not expert which are medium, one must wait until small ones as is written siman 293, and see there what we wrote further on this matter. And per the aforesaid view of the Gra, immediately after sunset of the body of the sun over the earth it is complete bein hashemashot, as stated. And in truth this view of his is not new, for Maharam Alshakar already agreed thus in responsum siman 96 that immediately after sunset of the body of the sun it is complete bein hashemashot, and he brought there that thus explicitly wrote the early Geonim in their responsa; they are Rabbeinu Sherira Gaon and Rav Hai Gaon and Rabbeinu Nissim Gaon; also R' Avraham HaChasid son of Rambam z"l also wrote there that thus is implied from the Rif and Rambam and Rashi, see there; and Shach brought it for halachah in Yoreh De'ah siman 266 seif katan 11 regarding the matter of bein hashemashot; and see also in the commentary of Maharalbach on chapter 2 of Hilchot Kiddush HaChodesh of Rambam s.v. klal ha'oleh that he also wrote that from the Rif and Rambam it is implied that he holds that from the beginning of sunset [namely when the sun is hidden from our eyes] it is bein hashemashot; and also Maharal of Prague in his chiddushim on Shabbos explained exactly like the aforesaid view of the Gra; and also Ra'avan holds thus that immediately when the body of the sun sets and is hidden from our eyes the time of bein hashemashot begins, see Hagahot Mordechai chapter 2 of Shabbos; and also in Sefer Seder Zmanim he extended and ruled for practical law like the Gra z"l that immediately after the beginning of sunset it is bein hashemashot. And behold for practical law one must certainly be careful per the view of the Gra and many of the Rishonim and poskim mentioned above that immediately after the beginning of sunset (namely from the hour when the sun is hidden from our eyes) it is a complete prohibition not to perform melacha, and Heaven forbid to be lenient in this, for it is safek issur skilah per the view of all these great authorities [and especially in our days when the world is not expert in the time of bein hashemashot; and in this manner for all there is to be stringent to refrain from melacha from the beginning of sunset as is stated in the Gemara and brought in Shulchan Aruch seif 3]; and it is not specifically regarding Shabbos, for the same applies to every matter in the Torah where there is a difference between day and night; we go to be stringent that immediately at the beginning of sunset bein hashemashot begins and the time of bein hashemashot continues until the emergence of three medium-sized stars, as stated. And know that in Sefer Yere'im of Rabbeinu Eliezer MiMitz was even more stringent regarding the beginning of bein hashemashot, and he holds that bein hashemashot begins three-quarters of a mil before the beginning of sunset, and his words are brought in Agudah and in Mordechai chapter 2 of Shabbos; and see in Bach who extended on this, and his view is that one should be careful l'chatchila to practice like the view of the Yere'im, see there, and he brought that thus was the custom of the communities from ancient times; and see in Magen Avraham who also brought the words of Bach, and it is implied from him that stringently he was concerned for the words of Bach [even though in the fundamental law he holds like Magen Avraham like the view of Rabbeinu Tam as is proven below siman 331 seif 5 in what is written there regarding milah on erev Shabbos]; however the Gra rejected the view of the Ra'avan mentioned above, and see in Sefer Seder Zmanim what he wrote explicitly on the words of the Ra'avan; and nevertheless l'chatchila it is certainly good to be concerned for the words of the Ra'avan and to advance a little more in kindling the candles in order to satisfy his view as well, as I wrote in Mishna Berurah seif katan 23, and as Bach wrote that thus was the custom of the communities from ancient times:
(3) That it is 3 milin and a quarter; see in Peri Megadim that the 4 milin are equidistant hours and not temporal hours; if so accordingly even during the period of Tammuz this measure applies as well; however in Sefer Minchat Cohen his view for halachah is that even per the view of Rabbeinu Tam the four milin are temporal, and in summer days it lengthens more, and the words of the Gemara were stated only during the time of Nissan and Tishrei when days and nights are equal, whereas on other days the matter changes per the time [but for practical law he concludes there that one should not rely on this reasoning except to be stringent, such as on Motzei Shabbos and not to be lenient]; and likewise it is implied from what Magen Avraham wrote in the name of Mahari"l that regarding accepting Shabbos it is obvious that we follow each day after its hours [meaning that the time from alot hashachar until the emergence of the stars of Shabbos, within which is also included the time of 4 milin after its hours]; and likewise is also the view of the Gra in his Biur that all the measures of the Gemara; whether the 4 milin which is until the emergence of all the stars according to his view, or the three-quarters of a mil which is the time of bein hashemashot; all are in the time of Nissan and Tishrei, whereas at another time it changes per the time, and in summer days bein hashemashot lengthens much more; and likewise the Gra wrote further that the measures of the Gemara were stated only on the horizon of Babylonia, but in our countries which incline toward the north bein hashemashot always lengthens more; and likewise wrote Sefer Minchat Cohen; and who in our time can precisely determine the time; therefore on Motzei Shabbos one must be very careful even per the view of the Geonim and the Gra not to perform melacha until three medium-sized stars are seen, for this is the clear sign of night stated in the Gemara in several places [Berachot 2a and Pesachim 2a and Megillah 20b], and before then it is not certainly night; and this sign applies in every place and at every time, but because we are not expert in medium ones we need small ones as below, and see in siman 293 what we wrote regarding the upper redness equaling the lower, which also applies regarding Motzei Shabbos. And per the view of Rabbeinu Tam one must wait on Motzei Shabbos from performing melacha until the time of 4 milin, which is at least the measure of an hour and a fifth from the time of the beginning of sunset, which according to his view is then the time of emergence of three medium-sized stars; and it is proper l'chatchila to follow the view of Rabbeinu Tam and all these great authorities who hold his view not to perform melacha on Motzei Shabbos until the measure of 4 milin is completed; and see what we wrote below in siman 293 in Biur Halacha s.v. ad at the end of the passage there. And regarding temporal hours on long days it appears that if one sees the upper redness equaling the lower (namely the red glow sank from the entire arch of the sky on the western side) and there are also three stars, one need not be stringent to wait for temporal hours on long days even per the view of Rabbeinu Tam [for behold these two signs are also stated in the Gemara [Shabbos 35] regarding the time of night, and it is also stated in the Gemara there that Abaye would look at the sign of the redness on erev Shabbos in the Gemara, and it is implied that with this sign alone he was satisfied; and although we are not as expert as they were, at least when the sign of the stars is also joined certainly we need not be more stringent; and better for us to say that we are not expert in the calculation of the horizons which change the sun in its marches according to place and time, and therefore we do not know well the calculation of the 4 milin which is only one sign, and we have what to rely on from the saying that we err in these two signs]:
(4) What time; see in Mishna Berurah what we wrote that it is not sufficient, etc.; likewise the Rash in Beitzah chapter HaMeivi and it is brought in Beis Yosef, and the poskim wrote that its measure was not clarified from the Gemara; and it appears that in any case it is less than the time of three-quarters of a mil [for otherwise the difficulty of Tosafos in Rosh Hashanah daf 9a s.v. v'Rebbi Akiva would remain, in what they challenged from that which is stated in Shabbos safek chashichah, see there]; and therefore I ruled anonymously in Mishna Berurah like the first view:
(5) And the measure of time of bein hashemashot, etc.; behold in Shabbos 35 we say the halachah is like R. Yehudah regarding Shabbos and the halachah is like R. Yosi regarding terumah, and the same applies regarding Motzei Shabbos as the poskim wrote; and ostensibly one should examine, since the reason of R. Yochanan who ruled thus is because of safek as is proven in the Gemara there, it is possible that we are stringent only regarding d'oraisa whose safek is l'chumra; but regarding all the shevutin, even if we hold that they decreed upon them during bein hashemashot, it is only during the bein hashemashot of R. Yosi; however from the closing wording of Shulchan Aruch it is implied that it applies also to the view that deals with shevutin which are d'rabbanan, and likewise is proven from Rama in the gloss in seif 1; and similarly it is implied in 35b in Tosafos s.v. hikshah, etc., see there at the end of their words; and likewise is proven from Rambam who wrote in chapter 5 of Hilchot Shabbos halachah 4 that from when the sun sets is the time called bein hashemashot everywhere; and in chapter 24 halachah 10 regarding the shevutin he wrote anonymously "during bein hashemashot"; behold it is explicit that from sunset which is the bein hashemashot of R. Yehudah the shevutin mentioned in bein hashemashot are forbidden. And indeed regarding a matter where we go leniently during bein hashemashot and we rely that it is night, such as regarding an individual fast [see in the Rash chapter 2 of Bava Metzia seif 24 and in siman 562 seif 1 in Biur HaGra there], it is implied from the words of the Rash, and likewise in the chiddushim of Rashba in the name of Rabbenu Yonah, that it applies even during the bein hashemashot of R. Yehudah; and accordingly regarding counting the omer according to those who are lenient during bein hashemashot in siman 489 it would be permitted even during the bein hashemashot of R. Yehudah; and likewise regarding shevut during bein hashemashot for the need of a mitzvah, where we hold in siman 302 that they did not decree upon it; per the view of the latter authorities who hold there that it applies even on Motzei Shabbos, it would likewise be permitted during the bein hashemashot of R. Yehudah, even though for R. Yosi it is still certainly day and not bein hashemashot. However one should examine according to what the Gra wrote in his Biur, and likewise in Sefer Korban Netanel; both of them were astonished at the Rash in what he was lenient regarding fasting because we hold stringently that the halachah is like R. Yosi, and if so according to him there is not even safek lailah before then, and we do not apply two leniencies to say that safek is permitted and the halachah is like R. Yehudah; for this too is safek; if so it is possible in our matter as well regarding shevut on Motzei Shabbos or regarding counting as well we do not apply leniency because of safek d'rabbanan, since for R. Yosi even safek does not exist:
(6) Before night; night is called from the Torah for every matter from when three medium-sized stars are seen; and because we are not expert between large and medium, therefore one must refrain from melacha even per the view of Rabbeinu Tam three-quarters of a mil before any stars are seen; and likewise Minchat Cohen, and it is straightforward. And know that as is known the measure of 4 milin changed per the horizon and time as is written above, and in our countries it is customary for stars to appear before the completion of the measure of 4 milin; one cannot perform melacha on erev Shabbos until the completion of the time explained in Shulchan Aruch even per the view of Rabbeinu Tam, for the day has already darkened at that time and it is night or at least safek lailah; rather he should refrain at least half an hour [which includes the time of bein hashemashot and tosefet Shabbos, as is written in Sefer Chayei Adam] before the time when it is customary for stars to appear in that place. And all this is per the view of Rabbeinu Tam; but we already wrote above that per the view of the Geonim one must refrain from melacha immediately after sunset when bein hashemashot begins:
(7) To advance, etc.; behold according to what the Mechaber wrote below in siman 459 seif 2 it is proven that he holds that 12 seasonal hours of the day are counted from alot hashachar until the emergence of the stars, and plag haminchah is an hour and a quarter before the emergence of the stars; if so there is nothing between the words of Rama and the earlier [view] except one-twentieth of the hour, for 4 milin are an hour and a fifth per the view of the Mechaber there, and from plag haminchah until night is an hour and a quarter; and it is known that a quarter exceeds a fifth only in twentieths. Afterward I found in Levush in siman 267 who raised this in any case, and see there that his actual view is that plag haminchah is an hour and a quarter before sunset; and see in Mishna Berurah:
(8) From plag, etc.; see in Peri Megadim who wrote that one who accepts Shabbos within the 4 milin is d'oraisa and in the positive commandment of tosefet Shabbos, and from this time until plag haminchah is only d'rabbanan:

dagul_merevavah.he: מחבר ובסי' שצ"ג ס"ב מביא ב' דיעות בזה ונרא' דשם קאמר שקיבל תוס' שבת ומיירי שאמר בפירוש שמקבל תוס' שבת א"כ לא קיבל רק איסור עשה משום הכי יש להקל בשבתות דאף שהפלוגתא במרדכי שהביא הב"י שם מיירי אחר עניית ברכו מ"מ המחבר הש"ע שם נמשך אחר לשון הטור שם אבל כאן מיירי אחר עניית ברכו שמן הסתם מקבל קדושת השבת ממש השמיט דעת המקיל:
dagul_merevavah.en: The Mechaber in siman 393 seif 2 brings two views on this, and it appears that there he is saying that one accepted tosefet Shabbat and it deals when he said explicitly that he accepts tosefet Shabbat — if so he only accepted a prohibition of positive commandment, therefore one is lenient regarding shevut; and the dispute in Mordechai which Bach brought there deals after answering Barchu; nevertheless the Mechaber Shulchan Aruch there follows the wording of the Tur there; but here it deals after answering Barchu that from anonymity one accepts actual Shabbat sanctity — he omitted the lenient view:

levushei_serad.he: <small>סק"ב</small> דעם חשיכה יאמר ערבתם ע"ח דהא ההיא מתניתין כצ"ל:
levushei_serad.en: Seif katan 2 — at darkness itself one should say "you made an eruv chatzerot," for that mishnah [deals thus]:

machatzit_hashekel.he: (ס"ק ב) אין מעשרין כו' וכ"מ ס"ס ר"ס. ר"ל מדהוצרך לשאול עם חשיכ' הפרשתם חלה מכלל דספק חשיכה אסור להפריש חלה. דאל"כ ה"ל להמתין בשאלת החלה עד ספק חשיכ' כנ"ל בסי' ר"ס בשם רש"י. ול"ל כמ"ש מ"א בסי' ר"ס גבי ערובי חצרות דוקא דיעבד הותר עירובי חצירות ב"ה משום מצוה אבל לא לכתחלה ז"א דע"כ בהפרשת חלה ליכא שבות כלל דאל"כ גם דיעבד לא היה מותר ב"ה דהא בהפרשת חלה ליכא מצו' ולא משום כבוד שבת דהא קי"ל חלת ח"ל אוכל והולך ואח"כ מפריש. וא"כ מאי כבוד שבת איכא בהפרשת חלה. ואי ס"ד דמותר להפריש חלה ב"ה ע"כ אפי' לכתחל' שרי דלית בה איסור כלל וא"כ תקשי למה הקדים לשאול על החלה עם חשכה אע"כ דאסור להפריש חלה ב"ה ומה"ט גופיה משום דליכא מצוה בהפרשת חלה דהא אוכל והולך ואח"כ מפריש ולית ביה משום כבוד שבת כנ"ל. ובחלת ארץ ישראל דאין לו תיקון ע"י שיאכל ואח"כ יפריש מודה מ"א דמותר ב"ה אם אין לו מה יאכל בשבת וכמ"ש ס"ק ו' לענין מעשר וט"כ ולכן סיים מ"א ס"ק זה וע' סי' תק"ו ר"ל בס"ק ח' שכתב מ"א שם אם חל ע"פ בע"ש ושכח ע"ש להפריש חלה מלחם חמץ דאין לו תקנה אפילו בח"ל לאכול ואח"כ להפריש א"כ כה"ג אם חל ע"ש בער"פ ושכח להפריש חלה מחמץ ונזכר ב"ה בע"ש מותר להפריש ב"ה דכה"ג הוי מצוה וכ"כ בספר ת"ש:
machatzit_hashekel.en: (s.k. 2) One may not tithe, etc. This is also implied at the end of siman 260. Meaning, since he had to ask while it was still daylight, “Have you separated challah?”, it follows that when it is doubtful whether night has begun it is forbidden to separate challah. Otherwise, he should have delayed asking about challah until bein hashmashos, as explained above in siman 260 in the name of Rashi. One cannot answer as the Magen Avraham wrote in siman 260 regarding an eiruv chatzeiros, that only after the fact was an eiruv chatzeiros permitted during bein hashmashos because of a mitzvah, but not initially. This is not so, because separating challah necessarily involves no shevus at all; otherwise it would not have been permitted even after the fact during bein hashmashos, since separating challah does not involve a mitzvah here, nor is it for the honor of Shabbos, for we rule that with challah outside Eretz Yisrael one may continue eating and separate it afterward. What honor of Shabbos, then, is involved in separating challah? If one were to think that separating challah during bein hashmashos is permitted, it would necessarily be permitted even initially, since it would involve no prohibition at all. The question would then remain why he advanced the inquiry concerning challah to while it was still daylight. Rather, it must be that separating challah during bein hashmashos is forbidden, precisely because no mitzvah is involved in separating challah here, since one may continue eating and separate it afterward, and it therefore does not involve the honor of Shabbos, as stated above. With challah of Eretz Yisrael, however, where there is no remedy of eating and separating afterward, the Magen Avraham agrees that it is permitted during bein hashmashos if he has nothing to eat on Shabbos, as he wrote in s.k. 6 regarding tithing and the like. The Magen Avraham therefore concluded this seif katan, “See siman 506,” meaning s.k. 8, where the Magen Avraham wrote that if erev Pesach falls on erev Shabbos and he forgot before Shabbos to separate challah from chametz bread, there is no remedy even outside Eretz Yisrael of eating and separating afterward. Accordingly, in such a case, if Shabbos falls on erev Pesach, he forgot to separate challah from the chametz, and remembered during bein hashmashos on erev Shabbos, he may separate it during bein hashmashos, because in such a case it is a mitzvah. The Tosefes Shabbos likewise wrote this.

magen_avraham.he:
שצריך להוסיף. והוי מ"ע דאוריית':
ג' רביעי מיל. והוא כמו רביעית שעה קודם צ"ה וב"ח כתב שיש להחמיר לעצמו כמ"ש ספר היראים ומרדכי והאגודה דמתחלת השקיעה הוי לילה וג' רביעי מיל קודם לזה הוי ב"ה וכן ראיתי זקנים ואנשי מעשה שפירשו ממלאכ' ב' שעות קודם שבת עכ"ל וז"ל תשו' מהרי"ל סימן קס"ג לענין תפלה וקבלת שבת פשיט' דאזלי' בכל יום אחר שעותיו דילפי' מחלקהו לשני ערבית וחשבי' לשעות מחצות עד הערב ומהנהו משערי' פלג מנחה ותוספת שבת ב' שעות לכל הקודם כדברי מהר"ח ויתישב בזה מנהג הקהילות עכ"ל ומשמע דחשבי' עד צ"ה ממש וכ"כ מנחת כהן ועמ"ש סימן רל"ג:
מפלג המנחה. והיא מהלך ד"א קודם תחילת השקיעה (תורת האדם) ובמ"כ כתב שט"ס הוא וצ"ל ד' מאות אמה בקירוב ובאמת היא חלק עשרי' מן השעה ואינו אלא כדי מהלך של"ג אמה ושליש, כת' רי"ו ה' יה"כ דאם קבל קודם פלג המנחה אין קבלתו כלום עכ"ל ומיהו כיון די"א דחשבי' מתחלת השקיעה בדיעבד יש להחמיר שלא לעשות מלאכה כמש"ל בשם הב"ח:
magen_avraham.en:
That one must add. And it is a positive mitzvah d'oraisa:

Three-fourths of a mil. And it is like a quarter of an hour before nightfall; and Bach wrote one should be stringent for himself as written Sefer HaYiraim and Mordechai and Agudah — that from the beginning of sunset it is night, and three-fourths of a mil before that is bein hashemashos. And so I saw elders and men of action who ceased from melacha two hours before Shabbat — end of his words. And these are the words of Maharil responsum siman 163 regarding prayer and accepting Shabbat — it is simple that they go every other day after its hours, for they divide it into two evening and night hours from midnight until evening; and from those they estimate plag mincha and tosefet Shabbat two hours for everything prior, per the words of Maharach. And through this the custom of communities was settled — end of his words. And it implies they calculate until nightfall literally; and so Minchat Cohen; and see what is written siman 233:

From plag hamincha. And it is a walk of four mil before the beginning of sunset (Torat HaAdam); and Machatzit HaShekel wrote it is a printing error and should read four hundred amah approximately; but in truth it is a tenth part of the hour, and is only the time of a walk of thirty-three amah and a third — as Mahari'v wrote — that if he accepted before plag hamincha his acceptance is nothing — end of his words. However since there is an opinion that they calculate from the beginning of sunset, b'dieved one should be stringent not to do melacha, as above in the name of Bach:

mishnah_berurah.he:
(יט) שצריך להוסיף - בין בכניסתו ובין ביציאתו וכדאיתא לקמן בסימן רצ"ג ס"ב עי"ש. ואין על הזמן הזה לא לאו ולא כרת כ"א מ"ע מה"ת וילפינן [בגמרא ר"ה ט'] מדכתיב ביוה"כ ועניתם את נפשותיכם בתשעה לחודש בערב מערב עד ערב תשבתו שבתכם ואמרינן יכול בט' מתענין ת"ל בערב אי בערב יכול משתחשך ת"ל בתשעה הא כיצד מתחיל ומתענה מבעוד יום כדי להוסיף מחול על הקודש וגם ביציאתו מוסיף מדכתיב מערב עד ערב ומדכתיב תשבתו שבתכם ילפינן דכל מקום שנאמר שבות כמו שבת ויו"ט גם כן צריך להוסיף ולשבות ממלאכה. וזמן תוספת הוא ע"כ קודם בין השמשות דבבה"ש הוא ספק שמא הוא לילה וחייב עליה אשם תלוי ולא צריך קרא לאוסופי:
(כ) מתחלת השקיעה - הוא דעת ר"ת וסייעתו דס"ל דשתי שקיעות הן מתחלה נכסית החמה מעינינו ושוקעת והוא הנקרא תחלת השקיעה ושוהה כדי ג' מילין ורביע מיל ועדיין יום הוא ומאז והלאה מתחיל השקיעה שניה שאז מתחיל להשקע האור לגמרי והוא נקרא סוף השקיעה ונמשך זמנה כדי שיעור מהלך ג' רבעי מיל שהוא אלף ות"ק אמות והוא בה"ש ואח"כ יוצאין ג' כוכבים בינונים שהם סימן ללילה ונמצא שלדעתו מתחלת השקיעה עד צאת הכוכבים היא ארבעת מילין ועיין מה שכתבנו בסמוך דהרבה פוסקים חולקין ע"ז וס"ל דמיד שנתכסה החמה מעינינו הוא בה"ש שהוא ספק יום ספק לילה:
(כא) רצה לעשותו וכו' - היינו ע"י דיבור שהוא מקבלו עליו לשם תוספת שבת או ע"י אמירת ברכו וכדלקמן בס"ד. ואם מהני לזה קבלה בלב ע"ל בסי' תר"ח ס"ג בהג"ה ובמ"ב שם. וע"ל ברס"ג ס"י בהג"ה דמנהגנו שהאשה המדלקת נרות לשבת היא מקבלת שבת בהדלקה זו:
(כב) איזה זמן - ולא סגי בהוספה כ"ש אלא שצריך קצת יותר. ושיעור התוספת עם בין השמשות ביחד עולה כמעט חצי שעה ועיין בבה"ל:
(כג) ג' רבעי מיל - והוא לערך רבע שעה. והנה השו"ע הזכיר בסעיף זה דעת ר"ת וסייעתו אבל הרבה מהראשונים ס"ל וגם הגר"א הסכים לשיטתם דבה"ש מתחיל תיכף אחר תחלת השקיעה היינו משעה שהחמה נתכסה מעינינו ונמשך זמנו כדי ג' רבעי מיל ואח"כ בסמוך לו יוצאין הג' כוכבים בינונים והוא לילה מה"ת לכל דבר. ולפ"ז יש ליזהר מאד שלא לעשות מלאכה אחר שהחמה נתכסה מעינינו ואפילו מלאכת מצוה כגון הדלקת הנרות לסעודת שבת ג"כ יזהר מאד לגמור הדלקתם קודם שתשקע החמה דלאח"כ הוא בכלל בה"ש ועיין לעיל בסק"ו. ולכתחלה אין להמתין עד הרגע האחרון רק יקדים הדלקתם משעה שהשמש בראשי האילנות כדלקמן ומי שמחמיר על עצמו ופורש עצמו ממלאכה חצי שעה או עכ"פ שליש שעה קודם שקיעה אשרי לו דהוא יוצא בזה ידי שיטת כל הראשונים. ולענין מוצ"ש עיין בבה"ל שבארנו בשם הפוסקים דלכ"ע השעור דג' רבעי מיל משתנה לפי הזמן והמקום ולא נאמר זה בגמרא אלא באופק בבל ובזמן ניסן ותשרי שהימים והלילות שוים ובמקומותינו שנוטה לצד צפון העולם מתארך הרבה יותר ע"כ יש ליזהר מאד שלא לעשות מלאכה במוצ"ש אף שנתאחר זמן רב אחר השקיעה עד שיראו ג' כוכבים קטנים וכדלקמן בסימן רצ"ג ס"ב ועי"ש במ"ב ובה"ל:
(כד) קודם הלילה - לילה נקרא מה"ת לכל דבר משיראו ג' כוכבים ועיין בבה"ל:
(כה) הרשות בידו - ונאסר בעשיית מלאכה אבל אם קיבל עליו השבת קודם פלג המנחה אין בקבלתו כלום ופלג המנחה נקרא שעה ורביע קודם הערב ועיין לעיל בסימן רל"ג דהוא שעות זמניות דהיינו בין שהיום ארוך או קצר מתחלק לי"ב חלקים וחלק ורביע קודם הערב הוא פלג המנחה. גם כתבנו שם דיש דעות בין הפוסקים אם שעה ורביע הזו הוא קודם השקיעה או קודם צאת הכוכבים ע"כ לעניננו בדיעבד אם קבל על עצמו לשם תוספת שבת עד שעה ורביע שקודם השקיעה יש להחמיר שלא לעשות מלאכה:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(19) That one must add (both at entry and at exit, as stated below siman 293 seif 2) see there. And upon this time there is neither lav nor karet, only a positive mitzvah from the Torah; and we derive [Gemara Rosh Hashanah 9] from what is written on Yom Kippur: "and you shall afflict your souls on the ninth of the month in the evening from evening until evening you shall rest your rest"; and we say: perhaps on the ninth they fast? Scripture says "in the evening"; if in the evening, perhaps from when it darkens? Scripture says "on the ninth"; how so? He begins and fasts from while it is still day in order to add from weekday onto the sacred; and also at exit he adds, from "from evening to evening" and from "you shall rest your rest" we derive that wherever cessation is stated, as regarding Shabbos and Yom Tov, one must also add and rest from melacha. And the time of addition is perforce before bein hashemashot, for during bein hashemashot it is safek perhaps night and one is liable an asham talui, and no verse is needed to add:
(20) From the start of sunset; this is Rabbeinu Tam's view and his supporters, who hold there are two sunsets: at first the sun is hidden from our eyes and sets, and this is called the start of sunset; it waits the measure of three mil and a quarter mil and still it is day; and from then on begins the second sunset when the light begins to set completely, and this is called the end of sunset; its duration lasts the measure of walking three-quarters of a mil, which is 1,500 amos, and that interval is bein hashmashos; and afterward come out three medium stars that are the sign of night; and it turns out according to his view from the start of sunset until the emergence of the stars is four mil; and see what we wrote nearby that many poskim disagree on this and hold that immediately when the sun was hidden from our eyes it is bein hashemashot, which is safek day safek night:
(21) If he wished to do it, etc.; meaning via speech that he accepts it upon himself for the sake of tosefet Shabbos, or via saying Barchu as below seif 4. And whether acceptance in the heart helps for this; see siman 608, se'if 3, in the Rama's gloss and Mishna Berurah there. And see siman 263 seif 10 in Rama's gloss that our custom is that the woman kindling Shabbos candles accepts Shabbos with this kindling:
(22) What time; and addition alone is not enough, rather one needs a little more. And the measure of addition together with bein hashemashot amounts to almost half an hour; and see Biur Halacha:
(23) Three-quarters of a mil; and this is approximately a quarter of an hour. And behold Shulchan Aruch mentioned in this seif Rabbeinu Tam's view and his supporters; but many of the Rishonim hold, and also the Gra agreed to their method, that bein hashemashot begins immediately after the start of sunset, namely from when the sun was hidden from our eyes, and its duration lasts three-quarters of a mil; and afterward near it come out the three medium stars and it is night from the Torah for all matters. And therefore one must be very careful not to do melacha after the sun was hidden from our eyes, and even melacha of mitzvah such as kindling candles for the Shabbos meal; also be very careful to finish their kindling before the sun sets, for afterward it is included in bein hashemashot; and see above s.k. 6. And l'chatchila one should not wait until the last moment, rather advance their kindling from when the sun is at the tops of the trees as below; and one who is stringent upon himself and refrains from melacha half an hour or at least a third of an hour before sunset; fortunate is he, for he fulfills thereby the method of all the Rishonim. And regarding Motzei Shabbos see Biur Halacha where we explained in the name of poskim that for everyone the measure of three-quarters of a mil changes according to time and place, and this was not stated in the Gemara except for the horizon of Babylonia and in the time of Nisan and Tishrei when days and nights are equal; and in our places that lean toward the north of the world it lasts much longer; therefore one must be very careful not to do melacha on Motzei Shabbos even if much time passed after sunset until small stars are seen, as below siman 293 seif 2; see there in Mishna Berurah and Biur Halacha:
(24) Before night; night is called from the Torah for all matters from when three stars are seen; and see Biur Halacha:
(25) He has the option; and he is forbidden in doing melacha; but if he accepted Shabbos upon himself before plag hamincha his acceptance has no effect; and plag hamincha is called an hour and a quarter before evening; see above siman 233 that these are seasonal hours, meaning whether the day is long or short it is divided into 12 parts, and a part and a quarter before evening is plag hamincha. We also wrote there that there are opinions among poskim whether this hour and a quarter is before sunset or before the emergence of the stars; therefore in our matter b'dieved if he accepted upon himself for tosefet Shabbos until an hour and a quarter before sunset he should be stringent not to do melacha:

netiv_chayim.he: <small>(ס"ק ו')</small> אבל לעשר ולהטביל הוא עצמו לא כצ"ל:
netiv_chayim.en: (s.k. 6) But to tithe and to immerse — he himself, not as stated:

peri_megadim.he:
ומערבין עט״ז שם כפירש״י ועמ״א ר״ס אות ג׳ וכפי הנראה דגירסת הש״ע בר״ס עשרתם הפרשתם חלה הדליקו הנר וכ״ה בלבוש השמיט ערבתם וכ״ה בש״ע של הנ״ץ ומ״ש שם דהמחבר השמיט ערבתם דלא נהיגין בי׳ א״כ אמאי הזכיר עשרתם דלא נהיגין ביה א״ו דבא״י נוהגין בזמן הזה עכ״פ מדרבנן כמ״ש המחבר בי״ד של״א ס״ב יע״ש וכ״ת מדרבנן יש שהות ביה״ש כמו דמאי הא ליתא דשבת קובעת מדרבנן ואפ״ה אין מעשרין ביה״ש ושאני דמאי רוב מעשרין כו׳ וכלי וולד הטומאה אפשר בימי טומאתו עמ״א שכ״ג אות י״א (בפרישה כתב ספק חשיכה אין מעשרין ודאי ואין מטבילין ע״י עצמו הא ע״י עכו״ם שיפריש מעשר ויטביל שרי אפי׳ הדלקת הנר מותר ע״י עכו״ם כו׳ יע״ש וא״י מעשר ע״י עכו״ם לא מהני בי״ד של״א ס״ל ומ״ש תרומה או מעשר) והסכים למ״ש המ״א ר״ס אות ג׳ דלכתחילה לא יסמוך עצמו בעירובי חצירות עד ביה״ש אלא אם שכח יכול לכתחילה לערב עירובי חצירות ביה״ש לא ע״ת וכ״כ הב״ח ברס״א ס״ג יע״ש ונתן תבלין לזה ג״כ דמסתמא בחד זמן נתנו חז״ל לשתיהם כא׳ ע״ח וע״ח שוב ראיתי דכוונתו להיפוך דודאי אז מותר לערב בפסק חשיכה יכול לסמוך לכתחילה ולהמתין עד ספק חשיכה אלא הואיל ע״ת א״א אלא עם חשיכה קבעו חז״ל לאמירה דע״ת ג״כ בזמן ההוא שלא ישכח אח״כ הואיל ומדכר חדא ולא אינך ומקשה שפיר בגמרא הא גופא קשיא ותיקן קושית הב״ח ברס״א ס״ג ועסי׳ שצ״ג בט״ז אות ד׳ ולשיטתיה כאן ושם ג״כ משמע דאף לכתחילה יכול להניח ביה״ש יע״ש וגם לתי׳ הב״ח ברס״א ס״ג מיתורא דמתני׳ נמי א״ש קושיית הט״ז שם ועתו״ש כאן ושצ״ג ולמ״ש א״ש. ומ״ש הט״ז ע״ת אין רגילין כ״כ עב״י וב״ח בפרט בדרין בין עכו״ם אין רגילין בע״ת ומש״ה השמיט המחבר בר״ס ג״כ ערבתם ע״ת וסובר ע״ח א״צ לומר עם חשיכה כמ״ש לעיל בזה:
בהג״מ כתב כו׳ עט״ז הגמ״י פכ״ג מה״ש אות ה׳ הביאו הר״ב לקמן שכ״ג ס״ז בהג״ה ומ״א י״ג בלא ברכה ולעיל כתבתי דביה״ש אפשר עדיף לטבול ע״י עכו״ם בלא ברכה דהוי שבות דשבות במקום מצוה ביה״ש אפשר לכ״ע לא גזרו. מ״ש בתשובת רש״ל ביא״ר ציי״ט דנזהרים הרבה הוי כצורך גדול יע״ש הביאו מ״א אות וי״ו לא מטעם מצוה:
בחדושינו שבת ל״ד א׳ כתבנו החילוק בין ע״ת לע״ח פירש״י הא אסמכיה אקרא וע״ח קיל טפי והנה מעשר וטבילת כלים יש לו שרש בד״ת מש״ה מחמירין ועיין מ״מ פ״ו מה״ע הי״ג דאין לבוא לבית הספק יע״ש ומכאן משמע דאסמכתא דיעבד שרי ולא אמרינן ביה ספיקו לחומרא ומיהו יש חולקין שם ועיין מהרש״א ז״ל ריש ביצה וספיקה אסורה די״ל אסמכתא מוקצה מש״ה החמירו בספיקא ואי״ה כשצ״ג ותט״ז יבואר זה וגם בפתיחה כוללת וכאן אין להאריך:
peri_megadim.en:
(א) And one makes eruv — Taz there as Rashi explained, and Magen Avraham siman 200 letter 3; and as appears the version of Shulchan Aruch in siman 200: "your tithe, your separation, challah, they kindled the candle" — and likewise Levush omitted "your eve," and likewise Shulchan Aruch of Netziv; and what he wrote there, that the Mechaber omitted "your eve" because it is not practiced on Yom Tov — if so, why did he mention "your tithe," which is not practiced; or that in Israel they practice nowadays at least rabbinically, as the Mechaber wrote Yoreh Deah 431 seif 62 — see there; and one could say rabbinically there is time during bein hashemashot as with demai — this is not so, for Shabbat establishes rabbinically and nevertheless one does not tithe during bein hashemashot; and demai is different, for most tithe, etc.; and keli-vlad hatumah — possibly during its days of impurity — Magen Avraham siman 323 letter 11 (in Perishah he wrote: safek chashicha one does not tithe definite produce and does not immerse by himself — but via a non-Jew who separates tithe and immerses, it is permitted; even candle lighting is permitted via a non-Jew, etc. — see there; and one could say tithe via a non-Jew does not help — Beit David 431 holds; and what he wrote terumah or tithe); and he agreed to Magen Avraham siman 200 letter 3 that l'chatchila one should not rely on himself for eruvei chatzerot until bein hashemashot, but if he forgot he may l'chatchila make eruvei chatzerot during bein hashemashot, not on Erev Yom Tov; and likewise Bach siman 261 seif 3 — see there; and he also gave seasoning for this — that presumably at one time the Sages gave both as one eruv chatzerot; and eruv chatzerot — I again saw his intent is the reverse: that certainly then one may make eruv at definite dark; one may rely l'chatchila and wait until safek dark; except since Erev Yom Tov is impossible except with darkness, the Sages fixed amirah of Erev Yom Tov also at that time so he not forget afterward, since one thing is mentioned and not the others; and he properly challenged in the Gemara — this itself is difficult; and Bach siman 261 seif 3 fixed Bach's challenge; and see siman 393 in Taz letter 4; and per his view, here and there also implies that even l'chatchila one may place during bein hashemashot — see there; and also for Bach's explanation siman 261 seif 3 from the mishna's source — there is no Taz's challenge there; and see Tosafot Shabbat here and siman 393 and what Eshel Avraham wrote. And what Taz wrote: on Erev Yom Tov they are not so accustomed via a non-Jew, and Bach especially among non-Jews they are not accustomed to Erev Yom Tov — therefore the Mechaber in siman 200 also omitted "your eve" on Erev Yom Tov, and he holds eruv chatzerot need not be said with darkness, as written above in this:

(ב) In Hagahot Maimoniyot he wrote, etc. — Taz, Gemara Mei'ut 323 Magen Avraham letter 5; Rambam brought later siman 323 seif 7 in Hagahah and Magen Avraham s.k. 13 without blessing; and above I wrote that during bein hashemashot possibly better to immerse via a non-Jew without blessing, for it is shevut and shevut in a place of mitzvah — during bein hashemashot possibly all agree they did not decree. From Rashal's responsa 218 that many are careful is like great need — see there; Magen Avraham brought s.k. 16 — not because of mitzvah:

(ג) In our novellae Shabbat 34a we wrote the distinction between Erev Yom Tov and eruv chatzerot as Rashi: behold I relied on a verse and eruv chatzerot is lighter; and behold tithe and tevilat kelim have root in Torah therefore they were stringent; and see nevertheless chapter 6 Hilchot Eruvin 13 one should not come to doubt — see there; and from here it implies asmakhta b'dieved is permitted and we do not say safek lechumra; however there are disputants there; and see Maharsha z"l beginning Beitzah that safek is forbidden — one could say asmakhta is muktzeh therefore they were stringent in safek; and it is not the place — siman 393 and Taz will explain this, and also in opening he included; and here is not to extend:

rabbi_akiva_eiger.he:
מג"א ס"ק ז' להדליק הנר קאי על דברי הג"ה קודם חשכה יכול לו' להדליק:
סעיף ב בהג"ה ואם רוצה להקדים בלבוש סי' רס"ג כ' דהוי כמו נדר ומהני לזה התרה ובא"ר פקפק ע"ז ועיין מ"ש בגליון סי' רנ"ג במג"א סכ"ו:
rabbi_akiva_eiger.en:
Magen Avraham s.k. 7 — to kindle the candle refers to the words of the Hagahah: before dark he can tell to kindle:
Seif 2, in the Rama's gloss. “If he wishes to begin earlier.” The Levush in siman 263 wrote that it is like a vow, and annulment is effective for it. Eliyah Rabbah questioned this. See what I wrote in my gloss to siman 253, on Magen Avraham, s.k. 26.

yad_ephraim.he: ס"ק י' והאמת הוא כצ"ל ר"ל שבאמת אין מפלג המנחה עד שקיעת החמה דהיינו תחלת השקיעה רק חלק ך':
yad_ephraim.en: s.k. 10 — and the truth is as stated, meaning truly from plag hamincha until sunset of the sun, namely the start of sunset, is only a portion of the day [time]:

mechaber.he: ומי שאינו בקי בשיעור זה ידליק בעוד שהשמש בראש האילנות ואם הוא יום המעונן ידליק כשהתרנגולין יושבים על הקורה מבעוד יום ואם הוא בשדה שאין שם תרנגולין ידליק כשהעורבים יושבים מבעוד יום:
mechaber.en: A person who is not knowledgeable regarding the measure (of bein hashmashos and does not know when to add to it) should kindle the [Shabbos] lights while the sun is still visible on the treetops. If it is a cloudy day, he should kindle them when the roosters sit on a beam while it is still day. If he is in a field where there are no roosters, he should kindle them when the ravens sit there while it is still day

biur_halacha.he: מי שאינו בקי וכו' - הוא תלמוד ערוך בשבת ל"ה ע"ב ולפ"ז בזמננו דבודאי לא קים לן ג"כ בשעורא דרבנן ובפרט בשבת דהוא מסור לכל בודאי החיוב ע"פ הדין לכ"ע להדליק קודם השקיעה. אח"כ מצאתי זה בשו"ע של הגר"ז שהזהיר מאד על הדבר עי"ש וכתב שם עוד דאם יהיה איזה אונס ח"ו שלא תוכל למהר להדליק עד שקיעת החמה אזי תצוה לא"י להדליק נרות של שבת והיא תברך עליהן הברכה ותבא עליה ברכת טוב ותקבל שכר על הפרישה עכ"ל ועיין לקמן בסי' רס"ג במה שכ' במשנה ברורה ס"ק כ"א בשם האחרונים שדעתם דאין לאשה לברך בזמן שהא"י מדליק:
biur_halacha.en: One who is not proficient, etc. This is an explicit teaching in Shabbos 35b. Accordingly, in our times, when we certainly are not proficient in the measure established by the Sages either, and especially regarding Shabbos, whose observance is entrusted to everyone, the obligation according to the law, according to all opinions, is certainly to kindle before sunset. I later found this stated in the Shulchan Aruch HaRav, who warned very strongly about this matter; see there. He further wrote there that if, God forbid, some unavoidable circumstance arises and she cannot hasten to kindle until sunset, she should instruct a non-Jew to kindle the Shabbos lights, and she should recite the blessing over them. The blessing of goodness will come upon her, and she will receive reward for refraining from kindling herself. End quote. See below, siman 263, regarding what the Mishna Berurah writes in se'if katan 21 in the name of the later authorities, whose view is that a woman should not recite the blessing when the non-Jew kindles.

levushei_serad.he: <small>(מג"א סק"א)</small> ואם נסתפק. אע"ג דבמ"ש גופי' ספק הוא והוי ס"ס לא מהני דספק חסרון ידיעה אינו כלום:
levushei_serad.en: (Magen Avraham seif katan 1) And if he is uncertain — even though in what is written itself it is safek and is safek sefeika, it does not help, for safek heser yeda is nothing:

mishnah_berurah.he:
(כו) בראש האילנות - או בראשי הגגות הגבוהים:
(כז) יום המעונן וכו' - וה"ה כשיש לו מורה שעות שהולך בטוב ויודע עי"ז אימתי הוא זמן השקיעה יכול לסמוך עליו [ברכי יוסף בסימן של"א]:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(א) At the tops of the trees — or at the tops of high roofs:
(ב) A cloudy day, etc. — and likewise when he has a timekeeper that goes well and knows through it when is the time of sunset he may rely on him [Birkhei Yosef siman 331]:

netiv_chayim.he: <small>(ס"ק י')</small> בקירוב כי היתרון הוא חלק כצ"ל:
netiv_chayim.en: (s.k. 10) Approximately because the advantage is partial, as stated:

mechaber.he: אחר עניית ברכו אע"פ שעדיין יום הוא אין מערבין ואין טומנין משום דהא קבלו לשבת עליהן ולדידן הוי אמירת מזמור שיר ליום השבת כעניית ברכו לדידהו:
mechaber.en: After the answering of 'Barchu', even though it is still day, one does not make an eiruv and does not insulate because they accepted Shabbat on themselves. And as far as he is concerned, where they say 'Mizmor Shir l'Yom Hashabbat' (before Barchu) it is like they said Barchu, as far as he is concerned.

baer_heitev.he:
מערבין. אפי' לדבר מצוה וה"ה דאסור ליכנס למרחץ אפי' להזיע ברכות דף כ"ז. עיין כנה"ג ובתשובת חכם צבי סי' י"א:
השבת. ובמדינות אלו אין נוהגין לומר מזמור ולכן עניית ברכו הוי קבלת שבת ד"מ. וכ"כ בסי' רס"ג ס"י. ועתה נוהגין לומר מזמור ואפ"ה אין מקבלין שבת ועושין כל מלאכות עד ברכו דמעיקרא הכי קבלו עלייהו. ב"ח מ"א:
baer_heitev.en:
Eiruvin. Even for a matter of mitzvah; and likewise it is forbidden to enter a bathhouse even to sweat, Berachot daf 27. See Kenesset HaGedolah and in responsum Chakham Tzvi siman 11:

Shabbat. In these countries they are not accustomed to recite the chapter of Tehillim [Mizmor Shir l'Yom HaShabbat], and therefore answering Barchu is acceptance of Shabbat per Darkei Moshe; and so in siman 263 seif 10. And now they are accustomed to recite the chapter of Tehillim, yet nevertheless they do not accept Shabbat and perform all labors until Barchu, for originally they accepted upon themselves thus. Bach; Magen Avraham:

beur_hagra.he: ס"ד אחר. תוספתא פ' בתרא דסוכה אע"פ שהמיחם בידו וברכו הוי קבלת שבת. ברכות שם הרא"ש ספ"ב דשבת:
beur_hagra.en: Seif 4, after. Tosefta last chapter of Sukkah: even though the kettle is in his hand, Barchu is acceptance of Shabbat. Berachot there; Rosh end of ch. 2 of Shabbat:

biur_halacha.he: אין מערבין - היינו עירובי חצרות כמו שפירשתי במ"ב וכן מפורש במרדכי סוף פרק במה מדליקין דהדין הזה נובע ממנו [ולפלא על הפמ"ג שרוצה לומר דהכא איירי המחבר בעירובי תחומין] ועיין במרדכי שם שרבינו יואל חולק ע"ז ומתיר והמחבר סתם פה כדעת המחמירין בזה [וכן הרמ"א בסי' רנ"ג ס"ב בהג"ה סתם להחמיר] והנה בשו"ע סי' שצ"ג ס"ב הביא פלוגתא בזה ומשמע שם דהוא נוטה יותר לדעת המתירים שסוברים דמה דהתירו בין השמשות הוא אפילו אם קבל עליו שבת ג"כ וכדי שלא יסתרו אהדדי מחלקים רבים מן האחרונים [הלא המה הא"ר לחד תירוצא והביאו הפמ"ג והמח"ב שהובא בשע"ת והשלחן עצי שטים] ואומרים דשם איירי ביחיד שקבל עליו שבת והכא דקבלת שבת של ברכו שהוא ע"י צבור חמיר טפי. ועיין בט"ז בסימן תר"א דפוסק דמותר לערב אפילו אחר שקבל עליו שבת וכן בדה"ח מצדד לפסוק דכל שבות לצורך מצוה מותר אפילו אחר שקיבלו הצבור שבת ואפילו בחצי שעה שקודם חשיכה והטעם דלא חמיר הזמן הזה מבין השמשות ובודאי לא היה דעת הצבור לקבל על עצמם התוספת שיהא חמיר מבה"ש עצמו עי"ש ומ"מ התוספתא שהביאו הפוסקים ראיה ממנה להחמיר אינה מתורצת בסברתו עיין במרדכי ועיין בבאור הגר"א בסימן שצ"ג ומשמע מדבריו דהוא מצדד יותר לדעת האוסרין והביא דגם דעת הרמ"א כן בסימן רנ"ג ס"ב בהג"ה. ומ"מ נראה לענ"ד דבהצטרף עוד איזה ספק יש להורות להקל בענין זה כגון שהוא שתי שעות קודם חשכה דלכמה פוסקים הוא קודם פלג המנחה ואין בקבלתו כלום ואף דמהרי"ו נקט לעיל בהג"ה שעה או ב' אפשר דלא נקטו רק לענין מלאכה דאורייתא של הדלקה דחל קבלתו ואין מותר רק ע"י א"י אבל לענין שבות במקום מצוה יש להקל אפילו ע"י עצמו אם הוא שתי שעות קודם חשכה:
biur_halacha.en: One may not establish an eruv. This means an eruv chatzeiros, as I explained in the Mishna Berurah. It is likewise explicit in the Mordechai at the end of the chapter Bameh Madlikin, from which this ruling is derived. It is surprising that the Peri Megadim wishes to say that the Mechaber is discussing an eruv techumin here. See the Mordechai there, where Rabbeinu Yoel disagrees and permits it. The Mechaber rules here without qualification in accordance with those who are stringent, and the Rama likewise rules without qualification to be stringent in siman 253, se'if 2, in his gloss. Now, in Shulchan Aruch, siman 393, se'if 2, the Mechaber cites a dispute concerning this matter, and it appears there that he inclines more toward the permissive view. They maintain that the permission granted during bein hashmashos applies even when one has already accepted Shabbos upon himself. To avoid a contradiction between the rulings, many later authorities, namely the Eliyah Rabbah in one of his resolutions, as cited by the Peri Megadim, the Machazik Berachah cited in Shaarei Teshuvah, and the Shulchan Atzei Shittim, distinguish between the cases. They explain that there the case concerns an individual who accepted Shabbos upon himself, whereas here it concerns the communal acceptance of Shabbos through Barechu, which is more stringent. See the Taz in siman 601, who rules that one may establish an eruv even after accepting Shabbos. The Derech HaChaim likewise inclines to rule that any shevus performed for the sake of a mitzvah is permitted even after the community has accepted Shabbos, and even during the half hour before nightfall. His reason is that this period is no more stringent than bein hashmashos, and the community certainly did not intend to accept an addition to Shabbos that would be more stringent than bein hashmashos itself; see there. Nevertheless, the Tosefta from which the poskim derive proof for the stringent ruling is not resolved by his reasoning; see the Mordechai. See also the Biur HaGra in siman 393. It appears from his words that he inclines more toward the prohibitive view, and he notes that this is also the Rama's view in siman 253, se'if 2, in the gloss. Nevertheless, it appears to me that when an additional uncertainty is present, one may rule leniently in this matter. An example is where it is two hours before nightfall, which according to many poskim is before plag haminchah, so that his acceptance of Shabbos has no effect. Although Mahariv above in the gloss mentions one or two hours, it is possible that he referred only to the Torah-prohibited melacha of kindling, regarding which the acceptance takes effect and the act is permitted only through a non-Jew. Regarding a shevus performed for the sake of a mitzvah, however, one may be lenient even to perform it himself when it is two hours before nightfall.

levushei_serad.he: <small>(ש"ע ס"א</small> מותר לומר לנכרי) דאמיר' לנכרי שבות ונתבאר בסי' שמ"ב דלא גזרו על שבות ביה"ש לצורך מצוה או שהוא טרוד ונחפז. ומה דאסור לעשר ולהטביל משום דלא מקרי מצוה דאם לא יאכל ולא ישתמש בכלי ליכא חיוב ומה דלא הוי נחפז משום שיש לו מאכלים וכלים אחרים משא"כ בשאין לו י"ל דשרי ובזה מובן דברי המ"א סק"ו:
levushei_serad.en: <small>(Shulchan Aruch, seif 1, one may tell a non-Jew.)</small> Instructing a non-Jew is a shevus, and it is explained in siman 342 that the Sages did not prohibit a shevus during bein hashmashos for the sake of a mitzvah, or when one is preoccupied and pressed. The reason it is forbidden to tithe and to immerse utensils is that this is not considered a mitzvah, since if he does not eat or use the utensil there is no obligation. Nor is he considered pressed, because he has other foods and utensils. By contrast, where he has none, one can say that it is permitted. This explains the words of the Magen Avraham in s.k. 6.

machatzit_hashekel.he: (ס"ק ד) ואין מערבין כו' דמיקני ביתא הוא ר"ל דכל אדם יש לו לילך מביתו וממקום שביתתו אלפים אמה לכל רוח. וכשרוצה לילך למזרח ביתו ד' אלפים אמה מניח ערובו סוף אלפים אמה מביתו. וה"ל כאלו קנה שם במקום ערובו שביתה ושם הוא ביתו. נמצא י"ל ממקום ערובו אלפים אמה לכל רוח א"כ מעירו לצד המזרח י"ל ד' אלפים. א"כ ה"ז דומה שקנה בית במקום שמניח העירוב וזה אסור ב"ה. משא"כ ע"ח דלא תקנו כ"א משום דהבתים שייכים כ"א ליחיד והחצר משותף בין כל בעלי החצר נמצא דחצר נגד הבתים דומה לר"ה נגד רה"י ואם יוציאו מן הבתים לחצר יטעו להוציא גם מרה"י לר"ה לכן תקנו ערובי חצירות דהיינו כל בית שבאותו חצר יתן פת תוך בית אח' שבאותו חצר ועי"ז הוי כאילו כלם דרים באותו בית ולא הוי משום קנין כאלו קנה אותו בית אלא משום דירה כאלו דרין כלם שם וא"כ כמו שהחצר שייך לכלם כן הבית דהא כלם דרין יחד וכן שאר הבתים נחשבו כאחד וכמבואר לקמן סי' שס"ו ולכן שבות זה דע"ח קיל מע"ת וכמ"ש סי' תקכ"ח אולם כן הוא בביצה דף י"ז דאין מניחין ערובי תחומין מי"ט ראשון לשני דלמיקנא שביתה בי"ט אסור. וכתבו התוס' אבל ערובי חצרות מותר דלא הוי קנין ע"ש. אבל כאן בפ' במה מדליקין אהאי דינא דהכא כתב רש"י ותוס' הטעם דע"ת דאסמכוהו רבנן אקרא חמיר משא"כ ע"ח דליכא אסמכתא קיל ע"ש:
machatzit_hashekel.en: (s.k. 4) One may not establish an eiruv, etc. Because this constitutes acquiring a residence. Meaning, every person may walk two thousand amos in every direction from his house and place of residence. When he wishes to walk four thousand amos east of his house, he places his eiruv at the end of two thousand amos from his house. It is then as though he acquired residence there, at the place of his eiruv, and that is considered his home. He may therefore walk two thousand amos in every direction from the place of his eiruv, and thus four thousand amos eastward from his city. This resembles acquiring a house at the place where he deposits the eiruv, which is forbidden during bein hashmashos. An eiruv chatzeiros is different. It was enacted because each house belongs to an individual, while the courtyard is jointly owned by all the residents of the courtyard. The courtyard relative to the houses therefore resembles a public domain relative to a private domain. Were they to carry from the houses into the courtyard, they might mistakenly carry from a private domain into a public domain. The Sages therefore enacted an eiruv chatzeiros, whereby every household in that courtyard contributes bread to one house in the courtyard. Through this, it is considered as though they all reside in that house. This is not based on acquisition, as though each person acquired that house, but on residence, as though they all live there. Thus, just as the courtyard belongs to all of them, the house also belongs to all of them, since they all reside together, and all the other houses are likewise regarded as one, as explained below in siman 366. The shevus of eiruv chatzeiros is therefore more lenient than eiruv techumin, as written in siman 528. This is indeed stated in Beitzah, folio 17, that one may not establish an eiruv techumin from the first day of Yom Tov for the second, because acquiring a place of residence on Yom Tov is forbidden. Tosafos wrote, however, that an eiruv chatzeiros is permitted because it is not an acquisition; see there. Here, however, in the chapter Bameh Madlikin, concerning the law stated here, Rashi and Tosafos wrote that eiruv techumin is more stringent because the Sages supported it with a Scriptural verse, whereas eiruv chatzeiros, which has no such Scriptural support, is more lenient; see there.

magen_avraham.he:
אחר עניית ברכו. בכ"ה כתב שיש מי שחולק ע"ז וס"ל דהתו' סוף סוכה שמביא במרדכי משבשת' היא דהא מותר להדליק הנר אחר תקיע' ג' כדמוכח בבריי' פ' ב"מ וכו' ואנו נקטי' כפסק הרב"י עכ"ל ולא דק דהמרדכי תקיעה שלישית שבג' אחרונות קאמר וכתב עוד שם דהמרדכי לא אסר אלא במי שקבל עליו שבת אבל מי שלא קיבל שבת אפי' אחר ברכו מותר בשבותין עכ"ל ולא עיין במרדכי סוף הפ' שהביא ראיה מהולכת שופר שהיא שבות עסי' רס"ג סי"ג:
אין מערבין. משמע אפי' לדבר מצו' אסור דהא טמונה לצורך שבת היא ואסור דגרע מב"ה וה"ה דאסור ליכנס למרחץ אפי' להזיע (ברכו' פ"ד):
מזמור שיר וכו'. ובמדינו' אלו אין נוהגין לו' מזמור וכו' ולכן ענית ברכו הוי קבלת שבת [ד"מ וכ"כ סי' רס"ג סי"ג] ועתה נוהגין לו' מזמור שיר וכו' ואפ"ה אין מקבלין שבת ועושין כל מלאכות עד ברכו דמעיקרא הכי קבלו עלייהו וכ"מ בב"ח סי' רנ"ז:
magen_avraham.en:
After the answering of Barchu. So he wrote; there is one who disagrees on this, and he holds that Tosafot end of Sukkah who brings in Mordechai from Shibulei HaLeket — that one is permitted to light the candle after the third tekiah — as is proven in the braita chapter 2 of Beitza — and we hold per the ruling of Rabbeinu Yerucham — end of his words. And he did not examine carefully, for Mordechai speaks of the third tekiah in the last three [blasts]; and he further wrote there that Mordechai forbade only for one who accepted Shabbat upon himself, but one who did not accept Shabbat — even after Barchu he is permitted in shevutot — end of his words. And he did not examine Mordechai end of the chapter who brought proof from walking with a shofar which is a shevut — siman 263 seif 13:

One may not establish an eiruv. It implies even for a matter of mitzvah it is forbidden, for the insulation is for the sake of Shabbat and it is forbidden, for it is worse than bein hashemashos; and the same applies that it is forbidden to enter a bathhouse even to sweat (Berachot chapter 4):

Mizmor shir, etc. And in these countries they are not accustomed to recite Mizmor shir, etc.; therefore the answering of Barchu is accepting Shabbat [Darchei Moshe and so too siman 263 seif 13]. And now they are accustomed to recite Mizmor shir, etc.; however they do not accept Shabbat and do all melachot until Barchu — for initially thus they accepted upon themselves — as Bach wrote siman 257:

mishnah_berurah.he:
(כח) עניית ברכו - משום דהוא התחלת תפלת ערבית של שבת לכך הכל פורשין אז ממלאכה וכדלקמן בסימן רס"ג ס"י דהוא כמי שקבל עליו קדושת שבת בפירוש ואסור אז בכל הסייגים והגדרים שגדרו חז"ל לשבת כגון לכנוס למרחץ להזיע בעלמא וכ"ש ברחיצה בחמין וכה"ג בכל השבותין ובא המחבר להשמיענו דאפילו אותן דברים שהתירו בבין השמשות כגון עירובי חצרות והטמנה דהוא בודאי לצורך שבת וה"ה כל שבות שהוא לצורך מצוה אפ"ה אסור כאן והטעם דכיון דקבל עליו שבת בפירוש אף שהוא זמן הרבה קודם ביה"ש חמור מביה"ש בלי קבלה [ולפ"ז לא יצוייר ההיתירא דבין השמשות הנ"ל לענין ע"ח והטמנה וכה"ג רק אם הוא במקום שאין שם צבור דאל"ה בודאי רוב הצבור קבלו כבר שבת בבין השמשות והמיעוט נמשכין אחריהן בע"כ וכמ"ש בסימן רס"ג סי"ב וי"ג ע"ש] ועיין בביאור הלכה בשם הרבה אחרונים שכתבו דדוקא ע"י ברכו שהוא קבלת שבת של ציבור אבל אם יחיד קבל עליו שבת מבעוד יום לא חמיר מבין השמשות וכן משמע ממ"א סק"ז:
(כט) שעדיין יום הוא - ר"ל אפילו הוא זמן הרבה קודם בין השמשות כל שהוא אחר פלג המנחה:
(ל) אין מערבין - אפילו לדבר מצוה:
(לא) כעניית ברכו - דמסתמא כיון שמזכיר שבת הוי כקבלה. וכתב המ"א ועתה נוהגין לומר מזמור שיר וגו' ואפ"ה עושין כל המלאכות עד ברכו [והיינו כשהזמן הוא קודם בין השמשות] והטעם משום דמעיקרא הכי קבלו עלייהו ואין מתכוונים בזה לקבלה. וכ"ז בזמן המג"א אבל במקומותינו המנהג כהיום מיד שאומרים מזמור שיר מקבלין הצבור שבת עלייהו ואסור בכל המלאכות אפילו עדיין היום גדול [פמ"ג ודה"ח] וכתב בספר דרך חכמה דה"ה במקומות שנוהגין לומר לכה דודי ומסיימין בואי כלה הוי קבלת שבת ממש ועיין בתו"ש:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(א) Answering Barchu — because it is the start of the Maariv prayer of Shabbat, therefore everyone refrains then from melacha, as below siman 263 seif 10, that it is like one who explicitly accepted kedushat Shabbat upon himself and is then forbidden in all the safeguards and fences the Sages fenced for Shabbat, such as entering a bathhouse to sweat in general, and all the more so bathing in hot water, and similar in all shevutin; and the Mechaber came to inform us that even those things they permitted during bein hashemashot, such as eruvei chatzerot and hatmanah that are certainly for Shabbat need, and likewise every shevut for mitzvah need — nevertheless here it is forbidden; and the reason is since he explicitly accepted Shabbat upon himself, even though it is a long time before bein hashemashot it is more stringent than bein hashemashot without acceptance [and therefore the permission of bein hashemashot mentioned above regarding eruv chatzerot and hatmanah and similar is only if he is in a place where there is no community, for otherwise certainly most of the community already accepted Shabbat during bein hashemashot and the minority are drawn after them perforce, as written siman 263 seif 12 and 13 — see there]; and see Biur Halacha in the name of many Acharonim who wrote that specifically via Barchu which is community acceptance of Shabbat; but if an individual accepted Shabbat upon himself from while it is still day it is not more stringent than bein hashemashot, and likewise is implied from Magen Avraham s.k. 7:
(ב) That it is still day — meaning even if it is a long time before bein hashemashot, all that is after plag hamincha:
(ג) One does not make eruv — even for a mitzvah matter:
(ד) Like answering Barchu — that presumably since he mentions Shabbat it is like acceptance. Magen Avraham wrote: and now the custom is to say Mizmor Shir, etc., and nevertheless they do all melacha until Barchu [and this is when the time is before bein hashemashot] and the reason is that originally they accepted thus and do not intend acceptance thereby. All this in Magen Avraham's time; but in our places the custom today is immediately when they say Mizmor Shir the community accepts Shabbat upon themselves and it is forbidden in all melacha even though the day is still great [Peri Megadim and Derech Chaim]; and he wrote in Sefer Derech Chachmah that likewise in places where they practice saying Lecha Dodi and conclude Bo'i Kallah it is actual acceptance of Shabbat; and see Tosafot Shabbat:

netiv_chayim.he: <small>(שם)</small> מתחילת השקיעה לכתחלה יש להחמיר כצ"ל:
netiv_chayim.en: (there) From the start of sunset l'chatchila one should be stringent, as stated:
